title: String to Integer (atoi)

understand.question: Given a messy text string, how do we parse a leading signed integer while skipping leading spaces, reading at most one '+' or '-', stopping at the first non-digit, and clamping to 32-bit bounds?
understand.plainExplanation: Think of a strict form-field parser walking left to right: first ignore leading spaces, then check for a single optional '+' or '-', then consume consecutive digits 0-9 until a non-digit appears, and finally clamp huge numbers to [-2^31, 2^31 - 1].
understand.inputMeaning: Any string s containing spaces, signs, digits, or letters.
understand.outputMeaning: The parsed integer clamped into [-2,147,483,648, 2,147,483,647], or 0 if no valid digits start after spaces/sign.
rules: Only leading spaces (' ') are skipped — once a sign or digit starts, spaces stop parsing too.
Only one optional '+' or '-' is allowed; two signs like '+-4' stops immediately and returns 0.
Unlike Reverse Integer (#7), out-of-range values are CLAMPED to INT_MIN or INT_MAX rather than returning 0.

terms.definition: Capping a value at the nearest boundary: anything > 2,147,483,647 becomes 2,147,483,647, and anything < -2,147,483,648 becomes -2,147,483,648.
A small state machine (start -> signed -> in_number -> end) where each character type triggers a predictable transition.

example1.whyValid: Skip the 3 leading spaces, read '-' (sign = -1), skip/absorb leading 0, read '4' and '2' (value = 42), then stop as soon as 'a' appears. Final answer: -42.

example2.whyEdgeCase: Massive negative number! Instead of wrapping around or returning 0, myAtoi must clamp at INT_MIN (-2,147,483,648).

steps.title: Phase 1: Skip leading spaces (indices 0..2)
steps.description: Advance index i past every leading ' ' until hitting '-' at index 3.

steps.title: Phase 2 & 3: Read '-' sign and digits '0', '4', '2'
steps.description: Read '-' (sign = -1, i = 4), then consume '0' (acc=0), '4' (acc=4), '2' (acc=42). Pre-overflow check passes on every digit.

steps.title: Phase 4: Halt immediately on non-digit 'a'
steps.description: Index 7 holds 'a', which is outside '0'..'9'. Stop scanning and return sign * acc = -42.

approaches.name: Single-Pass Pointer Scan with Pre-Overflow Guard
approaches.recommendedTradeOff: Scans left-to-right in O(n) time and O(1) space while catching 32-bit overflow before multiplication so it works identically in 32-bit and 64-bit languages.
approaches.coreIdeaSummary: Advance one index through spaces -> optional sign -> digits, clamping before overflow.
approaches.coreIdea: Walk index i sequentially: first skip spaces, then read at most one sign, then accumulate digits checking acc > floor((INT_MAX - digit) / 10).
steps: Advance i while i < n and s[i] == ' '.
Check s[i] for '+' or '-' to set sign (+1 or -1) and advance i by 1.
While i < n and s[i] is '0'..'9': if acc > (INT_MAX - d) / 10, return (sign == 1 ? INT_MAX : INT_MIN); else acc = acc * 10 + d.
approaches.whyItWorks: Checking acc > (2147483647 - d) / 10 guarantees acc * 10 + d never overflows 32 bits; if acc reaches 214748364 with d = 8 or 9 when sign == -1, returning INT_MIN (-2147483648) is exact!

approaches.name: Explicit Deterministic Finite Automaton (DFA)
approaches.coreIdeaSummary: Model parsing as formal state transitions: START -> SIGNED / IN_NUMBER -> END.
approaches.coreIdea: Define explicit states and a transition table mapping (currentState, charKind) to nextState so every edge case is handled cleanly by table lookup.
steps: Classify each character into space, sign, digit, or other.
Transition using the DFA table; on SIGNED update sign, on IN_NUMBER accumulate + clamp, on END break immediately.
approaches.whyItWorks: Separating state transitions from value accumulation prevents accidental fall-through bugs like accepting a second sign.
approaches.whenToUse: Great when writing industrial parsers with many character classes or explaining finite-state machines.
approaches.diagramNote: Characters drive transitions between states START (0), SIGNED (1), IN_NUMBER (2), and END (3).

diagram.caption: Any invalid character jumps straight to END and halts.
